title: Lovers of Pleasure More Than God
description: Lovers of Pleasure More Than God in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER OLD, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 36.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER OLD; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lo-vers of plea-sure more than God, For you he suff-ered pain; Swear-ers, for you he spilt his blood; And shall he bleed in vain?

lines: Lovers of pleasure more than God,
Swearers, for you he spilt his blood;
And shall he bleed in vain?
Misers, for you his life he paid,
Drunkards, your sins on him were laid,
That you might sin no more.
The God of love, to earth he came,
That you might come to heaven;
Believe in him that died for thee,
And, sure as he hath died,
Thy debt is paid, thy soul is free,

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to WINCHESTER OLD by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
